subject: chemistry
title: Alcohols
key_idea: (Separate science) Alcohols contain the –OH functional group. Methanol, ethanol, propanol and butanol are the first four. They burn, react with sodium, dissolve in water and can be oxidised to carboxylic acids. Ethanol is made from sugar solution by fermentation using yeast.

blocks.text: (Separate science) Alcohols are a homologous series of organic compounds. They all contain the same functional group, so they react in similar ways.

items.meaning: The atom or group of atoms that decides how a compound reacts.
A compound containing the functional group –OH.
A family of compounds with the same functional group and the same general formula, each differing from the next by CH₂.

blocks.text: (Separate science) Aqueous ethanol is made when a sugar solution is fermented using yeast. The yeast provides enzymes that catalyse the reaction.

items.meaning: The breakdown of sugar by yeast to make ethanol and carbon dioxide.

blocks.label: Fermentation of glucose
where: The reaction is catalysed by enzymes in yeast.

blocks.text: If the mixture is too hot, the enzymes are denatured and stop working. That is why the reaction is not carried out at 80 °C.

checks.q: State the functional group in alcohols and name the first four alcohols.
checks.a: The functional group is –OH. The first four alcohols are methanol, ethanol, propanol and butanol.

checks.q: Describe how ethanol is made from sugar solution. Name the process.
checks.a: Fermentation. Add yeast to the sugar solution and keep it warm and without oxygen (anaerobic).

checks.q: Write the balanced equation for the complete combustion of ethanol.

worked_example.question:
Methylated spirit contains ethanol.

Describe how ethanol is produced from sugar solution.

Give the name of this process.
answer_points: Anaerobic conditions (in the absence of oxygen) or warm (a temperature in the range 5–45 °C; room temperature is allowed).
worked_example.tip: One mark each: the name of the process, adding yeast, and one condition.

worked_example.question:
Propanol and butanol are both members of the same homologous series as ethanol.

Give three reasons why ethanol, propanol and butanol are members of the same homologous series.
answer_points: They all have the –OH group (hydroxyl group), the same functional group.
They have the same general formula, CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH.
Their formulae differ by CH₂ units.
They react similarly with oxygen, all burning to form carbon dioxide and water.
A trend in a physical property, such as an increasing boiling point, also scores.
worked_example.tip: Any three points score one mark each. Saying only that they are all alcohols is ignored, and hydroxide is not allowed.

extra.heading: Edexcel only: dehydration and concentrating ethanol

blocks.text: Alcohols can be dehydrated to make alkenes. Propanol and butanol are the unbranched forms, propan-1-ol and butan-1-ol.
Fermentation makes a dilute ethanol solution. Fractional distillation makes it more concentrated.

items.text: Put the dilute ethanol in a round bottom flask with a fractionating column and a thermometer on top.
Fit it to the top of the column and run water in at the bottom.
Heat above the boiling point of ethanol but below the boiling point of water.
Concentrated ethanol comes out of the end of the condenser.

method 2: catalytic addition of steam to an alkene

method 1
method 2

Ethene and steam: 300 °C, 6000 kPa (60 atm) and an acid catalyst.

worked_example.question:
Alcohols contain the functional group –OH.

Ethanol (C₂H₅OH) is an alcohol that can be obtained from glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆).

Explain why this process is carried out in the absence of air and at a temperature below 40 °C.
answer_points: In air, ethanol is not produced; the ethanol would be oxidised to ethanoic acid (vinegar), or carbon dioxide and water form.
Above about 40 °C the enzymes in yeast are denatured (lose their shape).
So the reaction slows down or stops.
worked_example.tip: Any four of these points score the four marks.

blocks.text: Ethanol can be made in two ways, and it can be oxidised to ethanoic acid in two ways.

items: Ethene and steam with a phosphoric acid catalyst, at about 300 °C and 60 to 70 atm.
Fermentation of glucose with the enzymes in yeast, in the absence of air, at about 30 °C.

blocks.text: Why fermentation uses no air and about 30 °C

items: Without air, ethanol is not oxidised to ethanoic acid.
At about 30 °C the enzymes work best.
If it is too hot, the enzymes are denatured and fermentation stops.
Microbial oxidation: ethanol reacts with oxygen in the air to form ethanoic acid.
Heating with potassium dichromate(VI) in dilute sulfuric acid also forms ethanoic acid.
